Method of Attack: Linux malware toolset consisting of an implant client coupled with a kernel module rootkit, a file transfer and port forwarding tool, and a Command and Control (C2) server
Client communicates with C2 infrastructure, uploads/downloads files, executes arbitrary commands with root privileges, forwards network traffic
Kernel module rootkit hides on infected machine and survives reboots unless UEFI secure boot is enabled in Full or Thorough mode
Communication between components via JSON over WebSockets encrypted with RSA
Stealthiness, persistence, complete access with highest privileges
Impacted Systems: Linux systems with kernel version below 3.7 or without UEFI Secure Boot enabled
Attack Vector: Direct communication with C2 infrastructure over network
Exploitation of Linux kernel module loading without signature enforcement
Indicators of Compromise: IP address linked to Strontium campaign and Drovorub C2 infrastructure (specific IP not disclosed)
Specific filenames, paths, hashes, Yara rules, Snort rules (provided in NSA report)
Network traffic patterns identifiable by NIDS like Suricata, Snort, Zeek via de-obfuscation of WebSocket messages
Presence of Drovorub kernel module detected by scripts and Linux Kernel Auditing System
Memory and disk image analysis artifacts
